title: Simulate Fiber Child & Sibling Pointer Linker
problemStatement: Implement `linkFiberChildren(parentFiber, childElements)` that takes a parent Fiber node and an array of child element descriptors, converts them into Fiber nodes, links the parent's `child` to the first child, links each child to its next `sibling`, and sets every child's `return` pointer back to `parentFiber`.
interviewTrap: Forgetting to set the `return` pointer on each sibling. The return pointer allows React to walk back up the tree without a call stack.

testCases.name: Links first child to parent.child
testCases.testFn: const parent = { type: 'div', child: null }; linkFiberChildren(parent, [{ type: 'h1' }, { type: 'p' }]); return parent.child.type;

testCases.name: Links siblings in order
testCases.testFn: const parent = { type: 'div', child: null }; linkFiberChildren(parent, [{ type: 'h1' }, { type: 'p' }]); return parent.child.sibling.type;

testCases.name: Sets return pointers on all children back to parent
testCases.testFn: const parent = { type: 'div', child: null }; linkFiberChildren(parent, [{ type: 'h1' }, { type: 'p' }]); return parent.child.return === parent && parent.child.sibling.return === parent;

details.name: Sets return pointers on all children back to parent

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: React represents UI as a singly linked list of Fiber nodes (`child`, `sibling`, `return`). Render phase is interruptible and can be paused; commit phase is strictly synchronous.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Fiber Tree Linking & Return Pointers.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Fiber Tree Linking & Return Pointers is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Forgetting to set the `return` pointer on each sibling. The return pointer allows React to walk back up the tree without a call stack.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.
